page: Amazon Web Services m7a.large is an entry-tier general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 2 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes AVX-512 vector extensions, including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, alongside AES and SHA cryptographic instruction sets. It lacks bundled local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, features no hardware GPU accelerators, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU capabilities contrasted against resource-constrained parallel throughput. The instance achieves top-quartile results in single-core stress-ng tests (3077.87) and Geekbench 6 single-core evaluations (1983.0), as well as strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression rates of 13.92 GB/sec. Conversely, overall throughput is limited by the two-core ceiling, yielding bottom-quartile scores in multi-core Geekbench (3579.0), PassMark CPU (5375.41), and multi-threaded decompression. Memory throughput shows average performance for large-block write operations (27.46 GB/sec) but drops to lower quartiles in read operations and PassMark memory benchmarks.

The qualitative cost-efficiency profile of m7a.large favors tasks that demand high individual core clock speeds and modern instruction sets over heavy aggregate compute. Because it features dedicated cores without simultaneous multithreading overhead, it avoids core contention at a modest infrastructure footprint. However, memory-bound workloads or models requiring substantial parallelism exhibit degraded performance, as demonstrated by weak 7B parameter LLM inference rates and reduced database operation scores.

The m7a.large instance is suited for lightweight enterprise workloads that do not require local NVMe caching or dense multi-threading. Typical deployment targets include small-scale microservices, low-traffic web serving, lightweight background task workers, code compilation runners with modest concurrency, and development environments requiring AVX-512 execution.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.large is a general-purpose Nitro-based instance configured with 2 dedicated x86_64 cores on an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. Equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, it maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The hardware environment lacks integrated local storage and GPU acceleration, while provisioning a 1 Gbps baseline network connection. Performance data reveals strong single-core compute results, reaching top-quartile metrics in single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests, aided by AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware flags. However, aggregate throughput is inherently bounded by the dual-core topology, resulting in lower scores on multi-threaded compilation, database operations, and larger language model inference. The instance delivers cost-effective resource efficiency for lightweight microservices, basic web hosting, small CI/CD workers, and environments prioritizing predictable single-thread execution over high core density.

tagline: Dedicated dual-core AMD EPYC compute with DDR5 memory, balanced resource allocation, and strong single-thread execution for lightweight cloud workloads.
bullet_points: Dual-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor operating at 3.7 GHz with dedicated physical cores
8.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory in a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio
Hardware support for AVX-512, SHA-NI, and AES instruction sets
Top-tier single-core benchmark performance counterbalanced by dual-core scaling limits
Zero bundled local storage and 1 Gbps baseline networking on the Nitro hypervisor
Suited for microservices, light web applications, and low-concurrency development environments
